title: Charter's End
subtitle: Thirty Days on Saltmoon, and the Company Wants Everyone Gone

listing.title: Charter's End 🧊
listing.blurb: A mining company has thirty days left on an ice moon, and it wants everyone off it by then, the people who were born there included. A driller is dead, the company says it was an accident, and the core she brought up holds something worth more than every ton of ore ever shipped. Levels 3–7.

synopsis: Esker, which everyone who lives there calls Saltmoon, is an ice moon of the gas giant Calyx at the cold edge of the outer system. For seventy-five years the Penwarden Combine has held the Claims Board charter to mine it. It cuts salt-laced ice and the heavy-metal sludge underneath, and throws the ore up to orbit with a magnetic launch rail called the Sling. The charter lapses in thirty days. The Combine isn't renewing it, because the ore is running thin, so it is closing Brinehold, the colony under the ice. Staff are going home, the last ore is going up to the bulk freighter Plainsong, and the Plainsong leaves at the lapse with everyone aboard. About two hundred of the people in Brinehold were born on Saltmoon or have lived there for most of their lives. They have no other home and they don't want to go. Two days before the countdown starts, drill lead Adaeze Rask dies at Bore Nine, sixty kilometres south on the fractured ice of the Shear. The Combine calls it a suit-seal accident and wants the inquest closed before the last shuttle lands. It wasn't an accident. Someone in operations released Bore Nine's depth interlock remotely and sent the drill down past the safety line into a pocket of the ocean under the ice. What came up in the core was alive. Saltlace is a mineral-and-microbe lattice from the brine sea, and its cold-stable proteins would change medicine across the system. Under Claims Board law, indigenous life must be reported and puts the moon under public trust. Under the charter's Article 9, if a hundred long-term residents are still registered on Saltmoon at the lapse, they become a recognised settlement and hold custodial title. So the Combine needs the death closed, the find unreported, the samples aboard the Plainsong and fewer than a hundred people left when the clock runs out. The player characters are the people who arrive, or who were already there, in those last thirty days.
hook: The shuttle Tern drops through Esker's sky of nothing at all, and Calyx comes up over the horizon. It is a banded amber-and-slate wall eighteen degrees wide, so close it looks like weather. Below, the ice is white and blue, cracked into plates like a dropped plate of glass, and in the middle of it is a cluster of domes and lights, and a launch rail running nine kilometres straight to nowhere. The passenger beside you is a pleasant man in a good coat. He says he is the Combine's close-out officer, here to 'help everyone home'. On the screen in the seatback a notice scrolls: BRINEHOLD CHARTER LAPSE: 30 DAYS. INQUEST, A. RASK, DRILL LEAD, BORE NINE: GALLERY HALL, 1400 LOCAL. ALL STAFF TO REVIEW EVACUATION ASSIGNMENTS. Underneath, someone has used a maintenance override to add a line in plain text, which the screen is trying and failing to delete: SHE DIDN'T SLIP.

setting.name: Esker (Saltmoon) and the Colony of Brinehold
setting.description: The outer system, far in the future: a long way from the sun, a long way from anywhere that matters, and seven weeks from the nearest station by bulk freighter. Calyx is a gas giant with forty moons, and Esker is the seventh: a ball of ice 1,900 kilometres across over a salt ocean, with a seventh of a standard gravity and a surface at minus 180 degrees. Calyx's tides flex the ice every orbit, once every three and a half days. Colonists call that the Turn, and it opens and closes the fractures of the southern Shear and drives up plumes of brine that freeze into falling snow. The Penwarden Combine's charter, held for seventy-five years, gave it the moon's minerals and the duty to keep its people alive. Brinehold is cut into the ice under the surface domes: pressure halls and work galleries lined with foamed insulation, kept warm by a fission plant in the Pumphouse. At its peak it held 1,900 people. Six hundred and twelve are left: 398 Combine staff on rotation who are glad to go, and 214 'long-stayers'. Most long-stayers are saltborn, people born under the ice to Combine families who never left. The rest are people who have lived there long enough that the outer system is their home. The Combine owns the air plant, the reactor, the uplink mast, the store and the housing. The colonists own their tools, their hall and each other.
setting.atmosphere: Cold, blue and close. Breath fogs in the corridors because the Combine has turned the heat down to save money. Everything is packing crates, chalked numbers and boarding lists. Calyx hangs in every viewport, banded and huge, and the light it throws is the colour of weak tea. Play it as a corporate thriller and a survival story. The enemy is a company, a clock and a moon that will kill you without meaning to. It is not a monster. Saltlace is wonderful, not frightening: it is a cold blue glow in a core sample, and the most valuable thing anyone in Brinehold will ever see. The Combine's people are not cartoon villains. Most of them are tired workers who want to go home, and the close-out officer believes in his job. Let the players feel the pull of both sides: some colonists want the buyout, and a decent manager made a terrible call under pressure. Keep the scale human. A union hall, a body on a slab, a heated argument over a ration of hot water, a crawler crossing a crevasse field in a storm. Show the clock all the time.

regions.name: Brinehold
regions.description: The colony under the ice. The Gallery is the long main hall: market, chapel, canteen and the colonists' meeting hall, where the inquest is held. Around it are the Warrens, the old residential cuts, tightly packed and threaded with crawlways, where the saltborn live. The Ledger House is the Combine's administration block, warm and well lit, home to Director Morrow's office, the records vault and the security post.

regions.name: The Pumphouse
regions.description: The fission plant, heat exchangers and water works under Brinehold's north end. Whoever holds the Pumphouse controls heat, water and air for the whole colony. The reactor is old, well kept and run by saltborn technicians who were trained by their parents.

regions.name: The Sling and Pad Row
regions.description: Nine kilometres of magnetic launch rail running north-east across the plain from the ore yards, which throws ore canisters to orbit for the Plainsong to catch. Beside it is Pad Row, the landing field for shuttles, crawlers and the last few surface vehicles. The Sling is the reason the Combine is still here, and stopping it is the only real leverage the colonists have.

regions.name: The Mast
regions.description: The Combine's high-gain uplink tower on a ridge two kilometres west of Brinehold. It is the only transmitter on Esker that can reach the Claims Board relay. The colony's own transmitter was dismantled as part of the close-out plan, so whoever controls the Mast decides what the rest of the system hears.

regions.name: The Shear
regions.description: The fractured belt of ice to the south, where the Turn opens crevasses, raises pressure ridges and drives brine plumes up into the black sky. Bore Nine is sixty kilometres in, the deepest drill site on the moon, three hours by crawler on a good day. There are not many good days on the Shear.

regions.name: The Plainsong
regions.description: The bulk freighter in high orbit: an independent hauler on Combine contract, 600 metres of cargo frame with a crew of eleven and a cold, practical captain. She catches the Sling's canisters and leaves at the lapse with the last of the ore, the Combine's records and anyone who has a berth. Her captain cares about her contract, her crew and her cargo, in that order.

campaignRules.name: The Charter Clock
campaignRules.description: The campaign runs on one public clock: C-30 (the day the Tern lands) to C-0 (the charter lapses at 0000 Brinehold time and the Plainsong breaks orbit). The GM states the day at the start of every session and whenever it changes, and never fudges it. Each scenario covers a span of days: sm-scenario-001 C-30 to C-27, sm-scenario-002 C-26 to C-13, sm-scenario-003 C-12 to C-6, sm-scenario-004 C-5 to C-0. The Turn comes every three and a half days (C-30, C-26, C-23, C-19, C-16, C-12, C-9, C-5, C-2) and brings quakes and plumes on the Shear (see The Ice). Fixed events: the inquest at 1400 on C-29; the Combine's 'comfort reduction' in the Warrens at C-22; Bore Nine recovery team leaves when the storm clears at C-8; the Article 9 register closes at C-1, 1200; the last Sling canister is thrown at C-0, 2200; the Plainsong breaks orbit at 0000. A day the party spends on something takes a day off the clock. Long travel and big plans eat days, and the players should feel each one go.

campaignRules.name: The Stayers
campaignRules.description: The GM keeps a public number, the Stayers: long-term residents (fifteen years or more) who have signed the Article 9 register and will still be on Esker at the lapse. It starts at 214 eligible and 140 signed. The colony needs 100 signed at C-1, 1200 to become a recognised settlement. The Combine is spending money and pressure to bring the number down. Typical changes: a buyout offer at the Gallery (-2d6, once per scenario), a cut to heat or water (-1d6), a frightening incident such as arrests, injuries or gunfire in the halls (-1d6), a colonist hurt by the party's actions (-1d4). A public win, like proof of the truth, a speech that lands or a cold shift helped through, adds +1d6, and a Face's Rally speech at a hall meeting adds +1d4 once per scenario. Say the number aloud whenever it changes. Named people count: if a companion or a pregen with fifteen years leaves, the players should feel it.

campaignRules.name: Notice
campaignRules.description: How hard the Combine is looking at the party, 0 to 10. The GM keeps it in world state and tells the players when it changes. It rises for being seen where you should not be (+1), for an alarm or an opened record (+1), for a confrontation with Combine staff in public (+1), and for gunfire or an injured Combine employee (+2). It falls by 1 for each full day without incident. At 3 the Ledger House security post logs the party's movements and Rook starts asking friendly questions. At 6 Halberd contractors are assigned to follow them, their door codes stop working and their shuttle and Plainsong berths are cancelled. At 9 Rook orders their arrest for 'interference with a charter close-out', which the charter lets him do and the Claims Board will review in about seven months.

campaignRules.name: Suits, Cold and Vacuum
campaignRules.description: Outside, nobody survives without a suit. A standard surface suit holds 8 hours of air, a crawler's tanks hold 72 hours for six people, and an emergency hood holds 20 minutes. Track suit air in hours. Suit breach (a critical hit from a blade or round, a fall onto sharp ice, or a failed DEX save DC 13 in an ice-fall): the suit loses pressure and the wearer is Bleeding until someone uses an action to patch it (no check with suit tape, Mechanics DC 12 without it). An unpatched suit fails after 3 rounds: the wearer makes a CON save DC 15 each round or drops to 0 HP. Cold: a suit with failed heaters, or someone outside the heated halls without proper clothing, makes a CON save DC 12 every hour or gains a level of exhaustion. Synthetics roll but have advantage. Inside Brinehold the halls are cold but survivable; after the Combine cuts the heat in the Warrens, a long rest there without the colonists' extra blankets restores only half hit dice.

campaignRules.name: One-Seventh Gravity
campaignRules.description: Esker's gravity is a seventh of standard. Everyone can jump three times as far and fall three times as far without harm: the first 30 feet of a fall do no damage, then 1d6 per 10 feet. Thrown objects go twice their normal range. Running is a long, bouncing lope, and stopping takes a turn. Without mag boots or practice, Athletics and Acrobatics checks to stop, turn or grapple fast have disadvantage. Saltborn, Spacers, and anyone who has spent a year on Esker ignore this disadvantage. Spacers' Thin Bones never applies on Esker. It does apply aboard the Plainsong, which spins at 0.8 g. Heavy things are light but still have all their mass: a crate that one person can lift will still crush them if it is moving.

campaignRules.name: The Ice: Crevasses, Quakes and Plumes
campaignRules.description: The Shear moves. On a Turn day roll a d6 for every 4 hours on the Shear. On a 1-2 the ice shifts: a crevasse opens (DEX save DC 13 or fall 2d6 x 10 feet; a roped team member makes the save with advantage; a crawler must make a Piloting check DC 14 or lose a track or a day), a pressure ridge shuts the route (a 4-hour detour, or Survival DC 15 to find a way through), or a quake shakes loose an ice-fall (DEX save DC 13, 3d6 bludgeoning, half on success). On a 6 a plume erupts nearby: brine shoots kilometres high and freezes, and for 1d4 hours the snow falls so thick that sight drops to 10 feet, suit radios hiss and navigation needs Survival DC 15 or the party wanders. On other days roll once per 8 hours, and only a 1 counts. A Scout's Trailwise or the colonists' ice maps give advantage on the Survival checks.

campaignRules.name: Guns Under Pressure
campaignRules.description: Brinehold is a series of pressure halls cut into ice and lined with foam, and every outer wall has vacuum on the other side. Any ballistic or energy shot that misses by 5 or more in a hall with an outer wall breaches it on a d6 roll of 1. Any plasma weapon or explosive breaches on a 1-3. A breach makes a howling wind toward the hole: STR save DC 13 or be pulled 15 feet toward it, the hall's pressure doors seal in 1d4 rounds, and anyone unsuited caught on the wrong side uses Suits, Cold and Vacuum. Guns are rare. The colonists have flare guns, a few old slug rifles for the surface, bolt drivers and cutting tools. Combine security carries stun pistols and arc batons. Rook's Halberd contractors brought caseless rifles and do not care about walls. Every shot fired in Brinehold, by anyone, is Notice +2 and Stayers -1d6. Make the players feel that a firefight in a hall full of families is a disaster even when they win it.

campaignRules.name: Evidence and the Claims Board
campaignRules.description: Two things can stop the Combine: a reported living find, which freezes extraction and makes saltlace public trust, and a death proven to be caused by the company, which voids the close-out indemnity and lets the Board appoint a trustee. Either one needs evidence the Board will accept, sent to the Board relay through the Mast. The GM tracks the pieces the party holds. For the death: Adaeze Rask's suit recorder (at Bore Nine); the Bore Nine interlock log (in the Ledger House vault, or recoverable from Wystan Corrie's partition, or from the survey lab's backup slate if nobody plays Wystan); and a witness (Ferrant Venn, Dr. Odalys Quarrie, or Director Morrow herself). For the find: a living saltlace sample (Bore Nine, or the Combine's sealed cold case, which goes up on the last canister); the core analysis (Wystan's partition, or the survey lab's backup slate); and a qualified signature (a Claims Board officer such as Sabeen Talwar, or a scientist). Any two pieces from one list make a credible report; all three make one the Combine cannot bury. A report that reaches the relay before C-0 counts. Evidence carried out on the Plainsong reaches the Board seven weeks after the lapse, and by then it is a court case that takes years.

explorationRules: Charter's End takes place on one moon over thirty days. Exploration means moving between a handful of places that matter and deciding how to spend each day. Inside Brinehold everything is close: Gallery to Ledger House is 5 minutes, Gallery to Pumphouse 10, and the Warrens' crawlways reach almost anywhere unseen if a saltborn shows the way (Stealth with advantage, Notice does not rise). Outside, everything is far and everything needs a suit. Brinehold to Pad Row and the Sling's ore yards is 20 minutes by surface tram or an hour's lope. The Mast is 2 kilometres west up a ridge: 40 minutes on foot, or a 10-minute crawler run that the Ledger House logs. Bore Nine is 60 kilometres south across the Shear: 3 hours by crawler on a good day, a day or more in a storm. The colony has two working crawlers, and the Combine controls both unless someone persuades or steals one. Each scenario gives the party more days than they need for any one thing and fewer than they need for everything. Let them choose. When they ask what is happening elsewhere, tell them: buyout queues at the Gallery, crates going up the Sling, a family arguing in a corridor about whether to sign. Show the Stayers and the Charter Clock whenever they change. The moon is never the villain. It is indifferent, beautiful and lethal. Calyx in the sky is the same every night, and the colonists navigate by it.
